events.quote: It would be novel for a court in this country to grant an injunction to hold up the effects of a judgment until the Court of Human Rights should rule on it, said the judge.

events.text: From a sale of land in the Vale of Glamorgan must be registered at HM Land Registry (SI 1975/160). The 1969 and May 1975 conveyances come before this date; the November 1982 sale of the fields comes after it.

events.title: Letter: Grievous loss
events.text: SIR,—The proposal for the ultimate demolition of the Great House Farm, Llandough, would unwittingly erase from memory one of the early historical sites of Glamorgan, marking, as it does, the location of the ancient Celtic monastery, a centre of first importance in the rise of Christianity in Morgannwg, comparable, indeed, in early record with the two other great Celtic monasteries of St. Cadoc at Llancarfan and of St. Illtyd at Llantwit Major.

events.title: ‘Open day’ to save ancient Welsh house
events.text: HUNDREDS of people yesterday flocked to see an 800-year-old house, containing centuries-old furniture and china, which is in danger of being demolished by developers.

events.title: Village green objection period ends (VG41)
events.text: The second objection period under the Commons Registration Act 1965 ends. It covers VG41, the land by Leckwith Road provisionally registered as a village green on 16 June 1970. Notice is given to the public only; the Act requires no personal notice to the occupiers of the farm.

events.title: “Cwm Cydfin Wood (Leckwith and Llandough)” in the Bute coppice-woods sale
events.text: Catalogue entry for the Bute coppice-woods auction including “Cwm Cydfin Wood (Leckwith and Llandough)”. Whether the soil or only the timber and coppice rights were sold, to whom and on what terms, is not in the catalogue.
Newspapers across Britain reported that the will of the third Marquess of Bute left the Leckwith-with-Llandough estate to his son, Lord Colum Crichton-Stuart.
src: Legal Wiki: EV-0012, Bute will press reports 1900

events.text: An industrial-history page traces the Llandough lime works and the brickworks next door, and notes the death of their owner J. E. Billups, reported in the South Wales Daily News.
src: Legal Wiki: EV-0292, Llandough lime works and brickworks

events.title: Daniel Thomas of Penylan dies
events.text: Daniel Thomas of Penylan, a contractor under Lord Bute and the owner of “valuable lime kilns at Llandough”, dies; his obituary appears in Tarian y Gweithiwr. In April 1888 a local man is described as “a labourer at Llandough Quarry”: the works beside the farm carry on.

events.title: “Llandough Home Farm”: the household of John Williams
events.text: 1881 census, Llandough, RG11/5288 p.2, schedule 9: the household of John Williams at “Llandough Home Farm”. The directories of 1868–1901 list him as “Williams John, Great house”.

events.title: Daniel Thomas & Son (Llandough Limeworks) is now friends with The Bute Estate
events.text: The agreement itself is not in hand.
src: EV-0291 · NLW Bute Estate catalogue D153 (Llandough limeworks land, 1876–1912)

events.title: Agreement with the Marquess of Bute over land at Great House Farm
events.text: Agreement, Marquess of Bute to Daniel Thomas & Son, 1877. The Bute deeds at the National Library of Wales describe “land (33 a.), formerly part of Great House Farm, for the Llandough Limeworks (33 a.), 1876-1912”.

events.title: Amy Williams
events.text: The Williams / Buckler family announces the passing of Amy Williams, relict of the late Mr. John Williams, Great House farm. She died at Llandough, near Cardiff, on 23 December 1864, aged 65.
The tithe apportionment for Llandough, Cogan and Leckwith recorded the owners, occupiers and field schedule of the parish, with the Marquess of Bute as landowner of Great House Farm.

events.title: “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”, 139a 3r 8p
events.text: David Stewart’s survey of the Bute estates in Glamorgan maps the farm on plan 19 as “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”, 139 acres 3 roods 8 perches.

events.title: The Bute Estate is now friends with The Vaughan family of the Great House
events.text: The Bute Estate acquires the freehold of the Great House in the early 19th century; the manorial courts for Llandough and Leckwith are then held in the house. The conveyance, and who sold, are not located.
src: Heneb HER GGAT02038s · Great House Farm (Vaughan freehold; Bute in the early 19th century)

events.title: The Bute Estate is now friends with Hurst & Jones
events.text: Purchase of the lordship by the Earl of Bute (Cardiff Records: Llandough’s later history follows Cogan, bought by the Earl in 1793).
src: Cardiff Records vol. 2, “The manors of Cardiff district” (Cogan; Llandough)

events.title: Hurst & Jones is now friends with The Herbert family
events.text: Inheritance by marriage: William Hurst and Calvert Richard Jones had married two heiresses of this branch of the Herbert family, and by 1767 held the manors of Dinas Powys, Llandough East and Cogan.
src: Cardiff Records vol. 2, “The manors of Cardiff district” (Cogan; Llandough)
